after.PASSED and VALIDATED: proposed to the owner as a paper strategy of its own (rule 14), on the US 500 CFD, twelve trades a year, sized by the risk engine, followed forward on paper; never real money
after.otherwise: reported as it is; nothing changes

spec.calendar: NYSE trading days computed from its rules and its unscheduled closures (scripts/phd1.py)
spec.data: Yahoo daily closes: SPY and IEF adjusted for dividends and splits, ^IRX as published (negative and zero yields kept); each file's sha256 in the manifest

gates.both_signs: the months it shorts and the months it holds long each have a mean net > 0
gates.costs_x2: mean net per month > 0 with the cost per side and the markup doubled
gates.development: mean net per month > 0, holds closing in 2003..2010
gates.t: t of the mean net return per month, holds closing in 2003..2018, >= the threshold
gates.top_year: no calendar year supplies more than 50% of the total
gates.validation: mean net per month > 0, holds closing in 2011..2018

spec.holdout_rule: holds closing in 2019-01..2026-09: mean net per month > 0 with one-sided t >= 1.645, and > 0 with the costs doubled

periods.membership: a month belongs to the period its hold closes in

spec.question: does trading the S&P 500 against the month-end rebalancing of 60/40 funds, from the close of the month's fifth-last trading day to the close of the next month's first, earn a positive net return at a CFD's costs?
spec.signal: the equity weight of a 60/40 SPY/IEF portfolio rebalanced at the previous month's last close, drifted to the close of T-4, minus 60%; short when positive, long when negative
